We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x)\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=8{x}^{3}\, & ⟹\,v=\int 8{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x=2{x}^{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 8{x}^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & =\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x)\cdot (2{x}^{4})-\int \frac{2{x}^{4}}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2{x}^{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x)-2\int {x}^{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2{x}^{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x)-2\cdot \frac{{x}^{4}}{4}+C \\  & =2{x}^{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x)-\frac{{x}^{4}}{2}+C \\  & ={x}^{4}(2\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x)-\frac{1}{2})+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.
